draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kannur! This is the land of Theyyam, where dancers become gods in firelit rituals through the winter. Down the coast, St Angelo Fort has guarded the sea since 1505.
draft.hungryLine: Kannur is famous for its biryani and its seafood. Here's where to start.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Visit St Angelo Fort, then the Arakkal Museum, then end at Payyambalam Beach.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit on Payyambalam Beach at sunset. It's long, wide and rarely crowded.
moodReplies.surprise-me: From December to April, villages around Kannur hold Theyyam performances through the night. Ask locals where one is on.

legends.title: Kerala's only Muslim kingdom
legends.body: The Arakkal family ruled Kannur and, for a time, the Lakshadweep islands. Their palace is now a museum.

legends.title: When dancers become gods
legends.body: In a Theyyam, the performer is believed to become the god. People come to them with their worries, and the god answers.

tips.title: Theyyam season is December to April.
tips.body: Most performances start late and run until dawn.

tips.title: Kannur handloom is famous.
tips.body: Buy straight from weaving cooperatives in town.

story.title: Port of the north
story.body: Kannur traded spices with Arabs and Persians long before Europeans arrived.

story.title: The Portuguese fort
story.body: Francisco de Almeida built St Angelo Fort, the first Portuguese viceroy's foothold on this coast.

story.title: The Arakkal kingdom
story.body: The Arakkal family ruled from Kannur and controlled sea trade.

story.title: The British cantonment
story.body: The British made Kannur a military base, and its weavers became known for their cloth.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Fort by day, beach at sunset and, if you're lucky, a Theyyam at night. Tell me what the god said.
